---
title: "The No Road Fallacy of Mathematical Symmetries"
author: "Galen Seilis"
date: "2023-12-20"
categories: [Mathematics, Symmetry]
draft: true
---

Suppose we have two cities $A$ and $B$ which we represent as two vertices of a graph with two parallel edges representing two distinct roads between them.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR

A o--1--o B
A o--2--o B
```

Let us also suppose that we have a space of metrics parametrized by the choice of edge (i.e. road taken) such that

$$d(A, B; 1) = d(A, B; 2).$$

Our symmetry here is that the distance between the two cities is invariant to the choice of edge
